title: Sly Dunbar - Wikipedia
notes: Lowell Fillmore 'Sly' Dunbar, born 10 May 1952, Kingston; died of cancer at home in Kingston, 26 January 2026. First record: Dave and Ansell Collins's Double Barrel; Skin, Flesh and Bones with Ansell Collins. His own words on his influences: 'My mentor was the drummer for the Skatalites, Lloyd Knibb. And I used to listen a lot to the drummer for Booker T. & the M.G.'s, Al Jackson Jr., and a lot of Philadelphia. And there are other drummers in Jamaica, like Santa and Carly from the Wailers Band, Winston Bennett, Paul Douglas, Mikey Boo.' Met Robbie Shakespeare in 1972; the Aggrovators for Bunny Lee, the Upsetters for Lee Perry, the Revolutionaries for Joseph Hoo Kim; Peter Tosh's band until 1981 (five albums). Right Time: 'because of that double tap on the rim nobody believe it was me on the drums'. Taxi Records from 1980. Bob Dylan's Infidels and Empire Burlesque, three Grace Jones albums, Herbie Hancock, Joe Cocker, Serge Gainsbourg, the Rolling Stones. Eno (1979): 'there's a 90 percent chance the drummer is Sly Dunbar'. Grammys for Anthem (1985) and Friends (1999); 13 nominations.

title: Sly and Robbie - Wikipedia
notes: The duo: the rhythm section and production team, the Taxi label, their work from the Revolutionaries to Black Uhuru, Grace Jones and Dylan.

title: Right Time (album) - Wikipedia
notes: The Mighty Diamonds' debut album (Virgin, 1976), recorded at Channel One, Kingston, produced by Joseph Hoo Kim; 'with the release of ...Right Time in 1976, the studio came into its own'. Personnel lists three drummers: Sly Dunbar, Leroy 'Horsemouth' Wallace and Anthony 'Benbow' Creary; Robbie Shakespeare and Ranchie on bass.

title: Aux armes et cætera (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Serge Gainsbourg's thirteenth album (spring 1979), recorded in Kingston with the I Threes; Sly Dunbar drums and arrangement, Robbie Shakespeare bass and arrangement, Mikey Chung, Dougie Bryan, Ansel Collins, Sticky Thompson, Robbie Lyn. The title track a reggae Marseillaise; sold over a million in 1979.

title: Nightclubbing (Grace Jones album) - Wikipedia
notes: Grace Jones's fifth album (Island, 1981), recorded at Compass Point, Nassau, with Sly and Robbie and the Compass Point All Stars.

title: Pull Up to the Bumper - Wikipedia
notes: Third single from Nightclubbing (June 1981); its rhythm recorded in 1980 at the Warm Leatherette sessions. Personnel: Sly Dunbar drums and syndrums, Robbie Shakespeare bass, Barry Reynolds and Mikey Chung guitars, Wally Badarou keyboards, Uziah Thompson percussion. Number two on the US dance chart.

title: Equal Rights (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Peter Tosh, 1977: Sly Dunbar drums, Carlton Barrett on African and Jah Guide; Robbie Shakespeare bass.

title: Sinsemilla (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Black Uhuru, 1980: Sly Dunbar drums, percussion, electronic drums; Spin on Sly and Robbie's 'trademark synth-drum grooves'.

title: Red (Black Uhuru album) - Wikipedia
notes: Black Uhuru, 1981: Sly Dunbar drums and syndrums; Sly and Robbie producing.

title: Sly Dunbar Intros (Serge Gainsbourg, Aux armes et caetera), transcribed by Todd Bishop
notes: Four pages, 2011 (pdf at pdxdrummer.com): the lead-in and first groove bars of fifteen tracks, 'a reggae drumming text book- nearly every track leads with an distinctive drum fill'. Rockers (the bass drum on every beat, hats in eighths, the snare on 3) on most; a galloping hat (two sixteenths and an eighth) on Les Locataires, Vieille Canaille, Ecce Homo and Toi Mourir; sixteenths on Mickey Maousse; syndrums marked in Vieille Canaille and Daisy Temple; timbale strokes in several intros; Negusa Negast with the snares off. Bishop: 'no written notation is going to do Dunbar's playing justice.'

title: Groovers and Shakers - Sly Dunbar (Mike Dolbear)
notes: A profile: the 2001 Right Time quote; 'In 1976, they experimented with a harder beat which was called "Rockers", which evidently replaced the then-prevalent "One Drop" style, then introduced the "Rub A Dub" sound in the early 1980s.' Dolbear met him around 1974.

title: Grace Jones - Pull Up To The Bumper (Songsterr tab 553021, drum track "Sly Dunbar")
notes: Human (aiGenerated false), revision 589342 by Juston Murphy, 2023; 51 bars at 109, three distinct: hats in sixteenths, the snare on 1 and 3 of the tab's bars, the bass drum on 2, its last sixteenth and the 'and' of 4, a wood block (GM 77) on every beat; the first bar opens the hat on its 1.
